title: Quad-layout seamless parametrization stage: 0.80 s to under 100 ms
description: Make the `seamless` stage of QuadLayoutEngine fast. It takes 0.800 s today. Breakdown: greedy integer rounding 0.259 (assemble 0.092, AMD 0.127, PARDISO factor+solve 0.040), injectivity loop 0.358. PARDISO's native load takes 0.41 s on its preload thread; check whether the stage waits on it. Related: PATCH-102. Baseline, measured 2026-10-15 with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --property quadLayoutScene.alpha=15` on the default model (headless, 9.1 s to ready): cross field 0.395 s, seamless 0.800 s, motorcycle graph 0.145 s, quantization 1.526 s, carve 0.674 s, contract 1.475 s, global grid map 1.897 s. These run synchronously before the scene's first frame, so together they are almost all of the quad-layout scene's time to first paint. The user's goal is first paint under 0.1 s; a sibling ticket moves the pipeline off the first frame, and each stage ticket makes one stage as fast as it can go. Target: this stage under 100 ms on the default model, or as close as the algorithm allows, with the reason it can go no lower. The stage's output must not change: same singularity count, arc/node/patch counts, quad count and a screenshot that image-diffs clean against the master baseline. Use the stage's own `[quad-layout] <stage>` log line and an async-profiler capture (`run-scene --profile`, read with `ixdar-cli profile-report`). Stay inside this stage's package; touch shared code (solver/, HalfEdgeMesh, QuadLayoutEngine) only where the stage needs it, and list every shared-file change in the report, because six sibling tickets run in parallel. Related: CRAW-2 (scan-scale pipeline), CRAW-4 (cached layouts).
definition-of-done:
1. The stage's `[quad-layout] seamless` time on the default quad-layout model is recorded before and after (median of 3 runs) in changes-made, with the after time under 100 ms or a stated reason it cannot be. 2. Singularity count, arc/node/patch counts and quad count match master exactly. 3. A screenshot of the final layout under tmp/ image-diffs clean against a master screenshot taken the same way. 4. No debugging scaffolding is left behind; `ixd wt done` passes.

5. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/<ticket> --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` covers sphere_base, sphere_random, bolt, hand, fandisk, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, Hand-tri-30k, rockerarm, buddha and the crawfish scan (~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, 8 GB heap). Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.

The pre-existing [injectivity] constraints=... log line stays: it moved from InjectivityConstraints.build to SeamlessParameterization.runInjectivityConstraintLoop so the side thread logs nothing; text unchanged.
testing-plan: 1. On master: run-scene quad-layout three times, record the stage time and counts, take a screenshot. 2. In the worktree: the same three runs plus a profile capture; compare times and counts. 3. image-diff the two screenshots. 4. mvn test for the touched packages.
unknowns: Whether the stage can reach 100 ms without changing its output; if not, what the floor is and why
changes-made: Baseline (worktree = master, machine-wide JVM lock, 3 cold runs botijo alpha=15): seamless 0.881/0.870/0.853 s, median 0.870 s. Sub-lines (median): dof system 0.024, rounding 0.254 (assemble 0.087, AMD 0.123, PARDISO factor+solve 0.043, n=29988, 0 candidates to pin), lazy round 0 0.324 (6 IPM factorizations), injectivity loop 0.402. Counts: singularities 72, layout nodes 446 / arcs 908 / patches 454, quads 14444. Screenshot sha256 22e54fa9... identical across runs. Warm JVM (model reloaded 4x in one JVM): seamless 0.53/0.43/0.40/0.34 s, so ~60% of the cold time is JIT warm-up. PARDISO preload finishes before the cross field ends on this model: the stage does not wait on it.

Change set (output bit-identical, botijo screenshot sha256 22e54fa9... unchanged): (1) SeamlessParameterization.resolve runs the greedy rounding and, beside it on a 2-worker Platforms WorkerPool, the solution-independent products: InjectivityConstraints.build and the MC19 projector's topology-only reduction (phases 0-4: alignment classes, branch walk, reduced matrix, integer IRREF), now done in the SeamlessProjector constructor; failures are captured and rethrown where the serial order raised them, and the [injectivity] constraints log line moved to the caller so the side thread logs nothing. (2) The injectivity loop reuses the rounding's base matrix (identical assembly: same face weights, no pins) instead of re-assembling. (3) AssemblyPlanBuilder.finish orders the per-face upper keys with two stable counting sorts (column, then row) instead of Arrays.sort plus one binary search per entry; same planUpperKeys and slots. After, 3 locked cold runs: 0.797/0.793/0.804 s, median 0.797 s (baseline 0.870). Unit tests QuadLayoutNodeChainTest, InteriorPointQpTest pass. No shared solver/ file changed.

Relaunch measurement (interleaved, locked, botijo alpha=15, cold): master seamless 0.863/0.879/0.870 s (median 0.870), worktree 1.004/0.755/0.634 s (median 0.755); counts and screenshot sha 22e54fa9 identical in all six. Probe of the IPM round: plan 0.026 s, condensed AMD 0.134 s, cold PARDISO factor ~0.05 s, 5 refactorizations ~0.016 s each. AMD reuse tried and rejected: constraint pairs add 2606 u-v entries to the 102123 base upper pattern (no exact reuse possible), and factoring the condensed system with the rounding's AMD ordering made each refactorization 3x slower (0.05 s vs 0.016 s, more fill) and changed the botijo screenshot. Reverted.

Cold-JIT finding: the Java AMD ordering of the 30k-unknown systems runs 0.12-0.15 s cold but 0.016 s once C2-compiled (4th repeat in one JVM, probe). Both AMD calls (rounding base system, injectivity QP condensed system) are therefore ~0.25 s of the stage. A background JIT warm-up (ordering a synthetic 170x170 triangulated grid 6 times at startup) was tried and did not help (real AMD still 0.12-0.15 s), so it was removed. Symbolic reuse: the QP already does one PARDISO analysis per lazy round and values-only phase-22 refactorizations after; botijo needs one QP round, and the rounding's symbolic factor cannot serve the QP because the condensed pattern and its AMD ordering differ. PARDISO preload: loaded 0.34 s after start, well before the seamless stage begins (cross field alone is 0.42 s), so the stage does not wait on it. No shared solver/ file changed.

DoD 5 suite (fresh, tmp/quad-suite/craw-67 vs master-0f52d26f): 14/14 MATCH, 0 differ. Seamless master -> worktree (single cold runs): sphere_base 0.046->0.024, bolt 0.576->0.315, hand 0.209->0.188, elk 1.002->0.874, feline 9.577->6.905, fertility 0.891->0.631, botijo 0.934->0.797, block 0.899->0.700, rockerarm 1.726->1.618, buddha 3.727->3.149. sphere_random, fandisk, Hand-tri-30k and crawfish are load-failed on master and worktree alike (same status, signature, screenshot), so the pipeline does not complete on them; seamless lines logged before the failure: sphere_random 4.891->2.52, fandisk 0.58->0.71, Hand-tri-30k 11.65->9.898. Unit tests QuadLayoutNodeChainTest + InteriorPointQpTest: 17 pass. Renamed SeamlessProjector.reducedColumnCount to reducedMatrixWidth (diagnostics scan flagged the Count suffix).
Archived 2026-10-16 without landing, as tag archive/craw-67 at 9d10b85e: Seamless stage only 0.87 -> 0.80 s on botijo; the cost is cold-JIT Java AMD ordering, not worth landing
